prose.text: Shift leads need a daily report showing short picks per picker so they can target retraining.
Sam spends four hours every Monday building the report in Excel from a WMS export; the WMS dashboard only shows building totals.
Automate a daily report per picker, ready by 6am, using WMS pick confirmations and including wrong-location scans.
No customer or pricing data; cancelled lines and over picks are not included.
If the report disagrees with WMS for two weeks, Sam will switch it off and revert to his spreadsheet.

acceptance.given: WMS pick confirmation data is available and processed for each picker per shift per day
acceptance.when: the report is delivered by 6am and matches WMS counts including wrong-location scans
acceptance.then: shift leads can use it to target retraining

acceptance.given: the report disagrees with WMS pick confirmations for two consecutive weeks
acceptance.then: Sam switches off the new report and goes back to his spreadsheet

guardrails.text: If the numbers in the new report disagreed with the WMS two weeks in a row I'd switch it off and go back to my spreadsheet.
Go back to the manual Excel process if the automated report fails or disagrees with WMS.

open_questions.question: Should wrong-location scans always count as short picks, and are there any exceptions?
Is 6am the final deadline for report delivery, or is there flexibility?

reflect_back_text: You want a daily short-pick report per picker, automated from WMS data and ready by 6am, so shift leads can target retraining. Today you build it manually in Excel, but the WMS dashboard only shows building totals. If the new report disagrees with WMS for two weeks, you'll switch it off and go back to your spreadsheet.
